# Carbon Energy Nexus

> A free daily publication at carbonenergynexus.com on where carbon, energy, water and capital meet: CO2 capture and storage, carbon markets and removals, energy policy, produced water and the water footprint of energy, project finance and research. Each edition sorts news by electrons (power), molecules (fuels), pore space (the subsurface) and water, tracks projects on a seven step ladder from announcement to operation, and says what each story means for investors, regulators, industry and founders. Facts are sourced and dated; stages and outlooks are labeled as our judgment. General information, not investment advice.

## Tools
- [Energy and carbon footprint calculator](https://carbonenergynexus.com/calculator.html): households and companies, EPA and EIA factors, transparent Nexus Score
- [Frameworks](https://carbonenergynexus.com/frameworks.html): how projects, policy and carbon claims are judged

## Today's edition
- [The EU and UK agree to link their carbon markets, with cross-border CO2 storage next in line](https://carbonenergynexus.com/): November 21, 2026. The EU and UK agreed on Nov 20 to link their carbon markets from 2028, recognizing each other's allowances and exempting traded goods from carbon border charges. Industry says cross-border CO2 storage could cut costs by up to 28%.
- [Capital: Finland's €300 million e-methane plant reaches a final investment decision](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#money)
- [Regulation: COP31 runs into overtime as fossil fuel and capture language divide countries](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#world)
- [Regulation: Alberta pays carbon capture grants during construction, as Pathways papers slip](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#alberta)
- [Regulation: Oregon and North Carolina make data centers carry more of their grid costs](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#power)
- [Water: Permian water networks change hands as treatment tries to beat the disposal well](https://carbonenergynexus.com/#water)
